title: Each step makes the next one easier

phrase.meaning: We will ease him toward hardship

points.label: What research comes close
points.text: **Al-Farrāʾ** (in al-Qurṭubī): when good and bad are paired, “easing” serves both, like “give them glad tidings of a painful punishment”. **Ibn ʿĀshūr** allows an ironic echo. **Ibn Kathīr** cites forebears: good’s reward is **the next good deed**, evil’s the next evil.
points.who: al-Qurṭubī; Ibn ʿĀshūr; Ibn Kathīr on 92:7–10

points.label: One possible reading
points.text: Verses 7 and 10 are identical except **one letter**: yusrā, ʿusrā. Neither road is drawn as a struggle. Giving and withholding both become **easier with practice**, so the person is shaped by the direction the first steps set.

bottom_text: For al-Farrāʾ the shared verb is only rhetorical pairing, and al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr place the easing in God’s decree, not in human habit.
source_label: al-Qurṭubī (citing al-Farrāʾ), al-Ṭabarī on 92:10 · Ibn Kathīr
